title: The text's word or the taught word
statement: Open: when pushing a student toward a stronger word, whether to push for the source text's own word or for the lesson's taught word when the text never uses it.
example: On one course's staging content, all seven word pushes the check flagged were taught words the story never uses.
detail: A content audit's closing-question checks ask whether a pushed word is genuinely stronger and the text's word rather than the lesson's (`shadow/content-eval/SKILL.md`). On staging all seven pushes the check flagged were taught words the story never uses, which departs from the specification's call for the stronger word the text supplies, so the check reports them as information until the choice is made. Nothing measured which push teaches better.

evidence.quote: It is `info` for Word Power words, because on staging all seven hits are taught words the story itself never uses.
**Is the pushed word genuinely stronger** than the likely child answer, and is it the text's word rather than the lesson's?
p16 step3 type blank uses `magic_word` gate with fuzzy synonym detection ("victorious", "winning" etc. trigger coaching toward the target word)
